content_sections.body: In this lesson, focus on contrastive stress on the corrected or preferred information. Notice how the ideas about documentaries and short clips are linked so that the listener can follow the speaker's meaning.
content_sections.title: Notice the language

content_sections.body: I do not dislike short clips, but I prefer DOCUMENTARIES when I want to understand a topic. Stressing documentaries corrects the idea that both formats are equally useful to me.
content_sections.title: Context and meaning

content_sections.body: Prepare a three-sentence response about documentaries and short clips. Include the lesson language, one concrete detail, and a clear link between your ideas.
content_sections.title: Guided use

items: The speaker gives no view or experience.
The speaker reaches the opposite conclusion.
exercises.prompt: Choose the statement that best matches the message about documentaries and short clips.
Complete this Emphasis and viewpoint sentence with a suitable linker: I have experience of this topic, ____ I can explain my view clearly.

Read the text: "I do not dislike short clips, but I prefer DOCUMENTARIES when I want to understand a topic. Stressing documentaries corrects the idea that both formats are equally useful to me." Then answer: Which format does the speaker prefer for understanding a topic?
Give a connected response about documentaries and short clips, then respond politely to one follow-up view.
exercises.rubric: States a clear experience or viewpoint.; Supports the main idea with a relevant detail.; Links ideas clearly and responds tactfully.

objectives: Use contrastive stress and opinion frames to highlight a viewpoint.

constraints: Keep transcript private until the first answer.
Ask exactly one question before revealing it.
Use no media; use only the supplied transcript.
listening.goal: Identify the main point and supporting detail about documentaries and short clips.
listening.instruction: Listen once to a short message about documentaries and short clips. Answer one question before seeing the transcript, then listen again for the linking language.

pronunciation.goal: Use sentence stress to make the main viewpoint about documentaries and short clips clear.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the key message about documentaries and short clips aloud. Stress the word that carries the main contrast or new information, first slowly and then naturally.

constraints: Use at most four tutor turns.
End after the learner has supported and clarified the main point.
speaking.goal: Complete a connected exchange about documentaries and short clips.
speaking.instruction: Discuss documentaries and short clips with the tutor. Give your experience or opinion, support it, and respond tactfully to one different view.

constraints: Do not replace the learner draft.
writing.goal: Write a supported B1 response about documentaries and short clips.
writing.instruction: Write 5-6 connected sentences about documentaries and short clips. Include a clear main point, a reason or example, and a tactful contrast. Submit your draft first.
